newsitem.title: USA: Stocks buoyed by technology shares, prospect of no Fed move.
newsitem.headline: Stocks buoyed by technology shares, prospect of no Fed move.

text.p: Stocks raced higher Tuesday, propelled by gains in technology shares and confidence that the Federal Reserve was unlikely to raise interest rates.

At 1:00 p.m. EDT (170 GMT), the Dow Jones industrial average was up 79.21 points at 7,882.56, building on Monday's 109-point rebound after Friday's dizzying plunge of 247 points on worries about the shape of future corporate profits.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 2-1 on active trading of 302 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, jumped 24.77 points at 1,594.29.
"We have had some encouraging news in the technology field and almost no chance exists that the FOMC will raise rates," said Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp.
The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee convened for its sixth interest rate meeting this year at 9 a.m. EDT (1300 GMT) and a decision was expected at 2:15 p.m. EDT (1815 GMT).
Bay Network was the most heavily traded NYSE stock, up 3-1/8 at 37 on the company's statement that it expected earnings above analysts' forecasts.
Stocks were also boosted by recovering bonds. The Treasury's 30-year bond rose 7/32, trimming its yield to 6.50 percent from Monday's close of 6.52 percent.
"The equity markets are going, to a great degree, to continue to follow the bond market," said Jim Pizzo, senior investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
Analysts said there was also an absence of any unpleasant surprises to rattle the market. Even the bitter 15-day strike at United Parcel Service was resolved overnight.
Gateway 2000 Inc. rallied sharply on news that UPS, one its main shippers, had resolved the dispute. Gateway's stock was up 2-3/8 at 40-3/16.
Investors were also scrutinizing the tentative agreement between United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union to end their 15-day strike for its effect on future inflation and corporate earnings.
Gillette Co.'s stock also rebounded, up 3-7/16 to 86-7/16 after last week's sell-off on earnings concerns.
But some analysts are concerned that the speed of the Dow's moves in the past few sessions has been too quick.
"We are trading within a range and working off, in a sideways motion, the excesses of the tremendous four-month run up," Stein said.

In the economic news, the Commerce Department reported that housing starts in July were at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.447 million, unchanged from June when starts increased a revised 3.2 percent from May. Wall Street analysts had forecast a slightly stronger 1.46-million-unit building pace for July.
